newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude buoyed by strong gas oil margin.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude buoyed by strong gas oil margin.

text.p: North Sea sweet crude markets stayed strong on Friday as high gas oil prices continued to provide ample return to refiners, but sour grades remained under pressure, traders said.
All four Brent dates to be nominated from the paper chains on Friday were kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline, illustrating the strength of demand for wet oil.
One North Sea equity holder said he was even getting interest in his mid-November cargoes, and was negotiating on the basis of floating prices.
"That says it will continue to be a strong market," he said.
November Brent was almost unchanged at $23.70/75 per barrel and the October/November spread steadied around +30/35 cents.

A Forties cargo loading on Oct 28-30 was sold at Dated Brent +45 cents, five cents firmer than the previous level, and Oseberg and Statfjord were both offered at +50 cents, again stronger than last done.
Brent found support from sales into the Mediterranean, northern Europe and possibly the U.S. Gulf.
But sour crudes remained under pressure, given the wide sulphur spread in gas oil markets.
"There is a general lack of interest in sours because of the high differentials for low sulphur gas oil," a trader said.
Plenty of Russian Urals from the Black Sea was on offer, but its value was steady at Dated -70 cents cif Augusta.
Loading programmes for November Nigerian crudes started to trickle out and signs were that Forcados would be in heavy demand for is high distillate yield.
Bids already approached Dated Brent +60/65 cents with sellers confident higher levels could be achieved.
